chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding a bondwoman who was divorced and then freed before her waiting period had ended, he عليه السلام said: "She observes an ʿiddah of three menstrual cycles. But if her husband died and she was then freed before her waiting period had ended, then her ʿiddah is four months and ten days."
ai.seo_question: What is the ʿiddah of a bondwoman who is freed before completing her waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the ʿiddah of a bondwoman who is freed before her waiting period ends. If she was divorced, her ʿiddah becomes three menstrual cycles; if her husband died, her ʿiddah becomes four months and ten days.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4872 - Ibn Abi ʿUmayr narrated from Jamil, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding a bondwoman who was divorced and then freed before her waiting period (ʿiddah) had ended.

Imam (as) said: "She must complete the waiting period of three menstrual cycles. However, if her husband died and she was then freed before her waiting period ended, her ʿiddah would be four months and ten days."
